## 1. Verdict: partly a fit

**Concept-first fits.** Approving a concept before painting is the normal process here:
- Nightshade's `paint/concept-05.json` records `"detail_model_approved": true` and `"final_masks_generated": false` before any masks were made.
- Crimson keeps `reference/approved-texture-concept.png` as the direction and says "Generated concepts guide the paint treatment; the Blender geometry is authoritative" (`art/ships/crimson/README.md:21`).

**A new neutral detail mask underneath the paint doesn't fit, for two reasons:**
- **No ship has one.** What each ship actually does, by your three categories:

  | Ship | Geometry seams | Generated brush shading | Authored mechanical detail |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Crimson | 39 separate parts | none; one hand-painted colour atlas | painted into `Crimson_BaseColor.png`, so it can't be recoloured |
  | Valis | separate panels | `ship_paint` Shadow/Light/Ink | none on file |
  | Nightshade | louvers are real strips (`marker-provenance.json` → `edge_light_cleanup`) | marker swaths projected into Shadow/Light/Ink | only green ticks in `Emission.png`. The marker prompt bans "new seams" |
  | Vanguard | n/a | n/a | the only real authored detail: `structural-lines.json` (14 tapered seam strips, 0.0048–0.0072 wide) and `service-panels.json` (hatch frame, cover, hinge, latch, 5-slat vent, 3 cooling slots, inner channels) |

  Vanguard built those as offset overlay meshes. In production the vent and panel colour was then baked into the hull atlas, "removing the overlay's triangular gray seams", and the overlay objects are hidden (`vanguard/drawn-study/README.md:62-65`).
- **"Underneath" would hide it.** The layer order is base colours and BaseRegion, then shadow, light, ink. BaseRegion is a "solid bone coat" (`bulwark/paint-settings.json:10,41-46`), so anything below the bone would be covered.

**What fits instead:** put the detail in the existing `layers/Shadow|Light|Ink.png` as owner edits. They are already grayscale and palette-independent. The tool saves edits as the difference from `layers/baseline/` and keeps them through reruns (`ship_paint.py:11-12`), which is exactly how the cockpit reflections already work (`bulwark/README.md:7`).

**Proposed detail set:** modelled on Vanguard's set, at Nightshade's restraint ("calm interiors"). Mirrored left/right; the shading stays asymmetric.
- 2–3 tapered secondary seams on each large bone/plum plate, continuing edge directions already on the plate.
- One access hatch per charcoal shoulder or side armor: outline, a hinge tick, a latch.
- One 4-slat vent bank per side on charcoal: a dark slot plus a light lip, like Vanguard's slat/edge pairs.
- Two retaining bands and a cap ring on each metal canister.
- One inset seam per tail fin.

That's about 12–15 elements per side. The hood stripe areas and the nose panel stay clear. No lights, since an indicator would add a colour outside the palette.

## 2. One alternative: a Vanguard-style data file
Describe the seams and patches in a `structural-lines.json`-style file and draw it straight into Ink/Light. **Upside:** placements are exact, editable and repeatable. **Cost:** a new rasteriser. Vanguard's producers were retired to `evidence/vanguard`, and the only built-in mechanism, `ship_paint`'s `accents`, handles only axis-aligned boxes in |x|,y,z per part (`ship_paint.py:301-312`). That works for slats and hatches but not tapered seams. Only worth it if the details will be regenerated often.

## 3. Simplification challenge
Do you need a new layer at all? The three masks plus the baseline difference already give editable, palette-neutral, rerun-safe layers. Also check whether "high detail" reads at game size: Nightshade judged its concept at 32–96 px ship lengths (`concept-05.json` → `review_thumbnails`). Any detail invisible at 64 px should be cut, not refined.

## 4. Red flags
1. **Observed:** "underneath the paint" conflicts with the opaque BaseRegion coat (above). The detail has to go above the coat in Ink/Shadow/Light.
2. **Observed:** Vanguard's overlay-mesh detail was rejected over seam artifacts. Don't fake detail with offset decal geometry; it also breaks your "no new geometry" rule.
3. **Observed:** the Unity BaseRegion binding ([#1018](https://github.com/amindell11/astronomical-home/issues/1018)) is still pending. Until it lands, the detail can only be judged in Blender, not in game. **Hypothetical:** image generation may draw vents or hatches as raised parts, which flat masks can't reproduce. The prompt below forbids that.

## Image-edit prompt
Use `final-top.png` as the edit target and `final-front.png` as a second reference:

> Image 1 is the EXACT edit target: the approved Bulwark paint. Keep the silhouette, every plate boundary, the camera, scale, background, plum/bone/charcoal colours and stripe placement, the asymmetric painted light and shadow, and the drawn cockpit reflections exactly unchanged. Add only flat, hand-inked mechanical detail drawn onto the existing surfaces, the same weight as the existing plate outlines: 2–3 thin tapered panel seams on each large bone and plum plate, following existing edge directions; one small access hatch with a hinge tick and a latch on each charcoal shoulder armor; one bank of 4 vent slats (dark slot plus a thin light lip) on each side's charcoal armor; two thin bands and a cap ring on each grey canister; one inset seam on each tail fin. Mirror the detail left and right. Keep the stripe areas, nose panel and plate centres calm. Nothing raised or carved: no new geometry, no lights, no new colours, no chips, scratches, wear, grime, rivets everywhere, text or decals, no realistic metal or gloss. It should read as a clean industrial-design illustration with structural line detail.

Nothing was changed. The next step is your approval of the generated concept.
